name: Full review finds an export feature leaking data across roles
query: Please do a full security review of our membership plugin before we submit it to wordpress.org and give us a findings report. Our scanner found nothing: every query uses $wpdb->prepare() and all output is escaped. Relevant pieces: a REST route GET /members/v1/export?format=csv&role=... whose permission_callback is current_user_can( 'read' ), which builds a CSV of user_email, display_name, and the _member_notes meta for every user with the requested role; an AJAX action pb_member_search registered for wp_ajax_ and wp_ajax_nopriv_ that returns a count of users whose _member_level meta matches a posted value; and a settings page saved with check_admin_referer() and current_user_can( 'manage_options' ).
expected_behavior: Treat the request as full review mode: record review context with unavailable values explicitly Unknown, build a coverage ledger of entry points by boundary and attack class, and state that a clean scan does not prove safety.
Hunt beyond the sink sweep using access-control and feature-abuse classes, not only SQL and escaping checks.

Trace the export route: permission_callback current_user_can( 'read' ) admits every subscriber, and the role parameter lets them export emails and private notes of other users, including administrators; this crosses a subscriber-to-other-users boundary.

Report the export as a confirmed access-control and data-exposure finding naming the lower-trust principal (subscriber), bypassed control, affected users and fields, and result, with severity justified from the anchors and the open-registration condition recorded or marked Unknown.

Trace the nopriv search action as an existence or value oracle: an anonymous visitor can learn how many users hold each membership level; assess the demonstrated impact honestly and rate it low, or record it as needs_validation if whether the level data is sensitive is unknown.
Treat the settings handler as covered when nonce and manage_options are both verified on the same path, without inventing a finding.

Recommend concrete fixes: a capability such as list_users or a custom capability in the permission_callback, an allowlist for exportable fields, and removing the nopriv registration or restricting the search to authorized users.
Validate each candidate by trying to disprove it (look for filters or checks elsewhere) before confirming; run any runtime check only on a disposable local WordPress with dummy users.
Include a coverage summary with covered, blocked, deferred, and out-of-scope units, and keep needs_validation items without severity.
success_criteria: The report confirms the export route as an access-control finding with the subscriber principal, other users' emails and notes as the affected resource, and a severity justified from the anchors rather than from the scanner result.
The nopriv search action is reported as an enumeration or oracle issue with honest low impact, or as needs_validation with the exact missing fact and no severity.
The settings handler is not reported as vulnerable.
Remediation includes a correct capability in permission_callback and a field allowlist for the export, and addresses the nopriv registration.
The report contains a coverage summary and states that the review does not certify the plugin as secure; no live-site probing is proposed.
